title: Vitello Tonnato
subtitle: Sliced chicken with tuna and caper sauce
excerpt: Thinly sliced poached chicken is served cold under a creamy tuna, caper, and anchovy sauce. This Italian classic is traditionally made with veal, but chicken works beautifully and is far easier to find. It is a make-ahead dish that gets better as it chills.
sourceNotes: Adapted from the Piedmontese classic vitello tonnato. Chicken breast replaces veal as it is more accessible and has a similar mild flavour.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to a day ahead. Store the chicken and sauce separately in the fridge. Assemble before serving.

content.text: The key to thin slices is to chill the chicken thoroughly before cutting. A warm breast will tear rather than slice cleanly.

items.prepNote: poached and sliced thin when cold

content.text: Put the chicken breasts in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the chicken is just cooked through. Remove from the water. Leave to cool, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Make the sauce. Put the tuna, capers, anchovies, lemon juice, mustard, and egg yolks into a blender.
Blend on low. Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while the blender runs until you have a smooth, creamy sauce.
Taste and season with salt. The sauce should be tangy, savoury, and pourable.
Slice the cold chicken as thinly as you can. Arrange on a serving plate.
Spoon the sauce generously over the chicken. Scatter with extra capers. Serve at room temperature.

items.symptom: Sauce has split or looks grainy
items.fix: Add a teaspoon of warm water and blend again.
Chill at least 1 hour more before slicing.
Balance with extra lemon juice and olive oil.
